Duke Energy Landlord Experience QUICK START GUIDE

The Duke Energy online Landlord Experience is designed for landlords and property managers to take care of their energy needs as quickly and conveniently as possible by:

Streamlining the bill pay process • Managing their properties related to tenant move-ins and move-outs • Efficiently keeping the right people in the know on energy-related matters, like outages • Tracking and managing energy usage and costs

GETTING STARTED

Registration for Existing Online Account Customers

Customers with existing online accounts can sign in using their current credentials and may find their accounts already set up in the Landlord, Business or Home tool .

Existing accounts that you have previously set up on a Revert-to-Owner program (to automatically reestablish service in your name when a tenant moves out) may find their accounts already established in the Landlord Experience. In this case, when you log in you will already see “Landlord” as an option for selection. (See Experience Selector to the right.)

Existing accounts on Residential rates that were not previously set up on a Revert-to Owner program may be set up in the “Home” experience .

Accounts with Nonresidential/Business rates will be

found in the Business tool .

Key Points

Registered users can manage multiple account types across different experiences using a single sign-in ID – for example, Home, Business and Landlord.

1 . If you have accounts in multiple tools, you will see an experience selector page when signing in (1).

2 . You can easily navigate back to an alternate

2 . You can easily navigate back to an alternate

experience by selecting the experience selector icon on the upper right portion of your dashboard within any of the tools (2).

3 . These setups are flexible, and accounts can be moved

to fit the way you want to work. If you want accounts set up differently, please contact our Business Customer Service team (duke-energy .com/customer-service/business) so we can help make that happen.

Start or Stop Service to a Property The Landlord Experience also allows you to start or stop service for eligible properties. Locate the ellipsis (three dots) at the far-right column of each property row to choose:

1 . Turn on Service – Applicable only when the service is

noted as Inactive (1).

2 . Turn off Service – Applicable only when a property is

noted as Inactive (1).

2 . Turn off Service – Applicable only when a property is

listed as Active Owner. If the property is listed as Active Tenant, the landlord cannot turn off service to that property (2).

Note: When service is active in tenant’s name, you will not be able to view the name of tenant or see if service has been disconnected for nonpayment .

Enroll/Unenroll in Revert-to-Owner The Revert-to-Owner (RTO) agreement is the formal contract into which a landlord enters when wanting service to automatically revert to landlord’s name when a tenant vacates a property . The landlord agrees to take responsibility for charges incurred for the period of time service is active in their name .

Enrolling a property in RTO can occur:

During initial registration/adding a property to the

Enrolling a property in RTO can occur:

During initial registration/adding a property to the

Landlord Experience .

On the Manage Properties page using the commands at the end of each property listing (see previous section) or through the ‘Manage Revert to Owner’ feature (1) .

Using the Manage Revert to Owner page to enroll one

or multiple properties at once .

Navigate to the Manage Revert to Owner page by selecting Services and selecting Manage Revert to Owner (RTO).

Key points related to RTO enrollment: • By selecting the Enrolled and Not Enrolled tabs you can

see which accounts currently fall into each condition. By selecting accounts with the check box and choosing Enroll or Unenroll as appropriate, you can move your accounts on and off the program (2).

You must review the Terms and Conditions of the RTO program and check the box to accept this information (3) . This box serves as the electronic signature acknowledging that you will adhere to all Terms and Conditions of the program (4) .

To enroll properties in RTO, the customer cannot have

a past-due balance on any other accounts .

STREAMLINE BILL PAYMENT

Pay My Bills Page

Upon signing in, the total outstanding balance on your account(s) will display in the dark blue frame. This will include all the outstanding billed amounts currently due . Click “View/Pay Bills .”

On the Pay My Bills screen, you can:

1 . Initiate the payment process immediately by clicking

Pay Now (1).

2 . View the detail for any of your accounts by clicking on

them (2).

Pay Now (1).

2 . View the detail for any of your accounts by clicking on

them (2).

3 . Select one, multiple or all accounts to pay. The total

will adjust based on the accounts you select. Then Pay Now to initiate payment for the selected accounts (3) .

Tip: If your account due dates are spread across the month and you would prefer to align them to one or two different times of the month for easier payment, use Pick Your Due Date to realign accordingly. Then you will be able to select all you want to pay in one transaction going forward.

Making Digital Payments

Once you select Pay Now, you will be guided through the process to pay your bill online, and you will be presented with several options:

Source of Payment:

»

Source of Payment:

»

If you are signed in to your online account, you can pay digitally for FREE using a checking or savings account (1).

» You may also choose to pay using the Speed Pay service through a vendor who will charge a fee for business accounts . This does provide the option of paying with a credit or debit card.

Consolidated or Individual Transactions: You also

have the option of sending a multi-account payment through your bank as one consolidated transaction or individual transactions for each account. If you want your payments consolidated into one bank transaction, check the Consolidated Payments box as shown (2). If you leave the box unchecked, each bill will process individually through your bank . As soon as your digital payment is processed, it will be immediately reflected in your account balances and your total amount due on the dashboard .

Billing and Payment Activity

Easily view up to 24 months of billing and payment history in one consolidated view.

1 . Select Bills to view the invoice amount and due date for individual or groups of accounts, as well as view a PDF version of the monthly bill (1) .

2 . Select Payments to view payments posted and the

status of those payments (2) .

2 . Select Payments to view payments posted and the

status of those payments (2) .

Note: If you want to narrow your view to only one account, select that account in the upper-right corner (3) .

Billing and Payment Programs

Billing and Payment Programs

Under the Billing tab, you can access programs that align billing and payment to fit your business. Selecting each of the programs below will take you to a page that shows eligibility and enrollment status and allows you to enroll or unenroll in that program for each of your accounts .

Paperless Billing – Move all your billing to this digital portal to eliminate paper bills. You can pull up PDF versions of your bills for the past 24 months at any time .

Autopay – Automatically pay your bill with a selected

payment method on the bill due date .

Pick Your Due Date – Set your monthly due date at a time that works best for your business. If you have multiple accounts, align them to the same due date to make bill payment easier .

Budget Billing – Manage your cash flow by leveling out your monthly bills to avoid seasonal highs and lows or spikes caused by unusual weather activity.

Billing, Payment, Outage and Service Notifications

The Business Experience has expanded the number and types of notifications you can configure for your business to bring relevant information to the right people in your company via text, email or automated phone message when:

Your new bill is ready to view

A payment is coming due

A payment has been successfully posted to

your account(s)

equipment damage

A planned maintenance outage will occur and we want

to notify you in advance

You’ve made a service request and we have status

updates for you

Under the Accounts tab, choose Preferences and Notifications. Set up your payment notifications in three steps:

1 . Update Your Profile: Notification options pull from the phone numbers and email addresses set in your main profile. You can add up to 10 email addresses and 10 phone numbers . Make sure you have updated your profile with the information needed before configuring your notifications (1) .

2 . Select Notification Recipients: Under Billing &

2 . Select Notification Recipients: Under Billing &

Payment, configure the combination of notifications that works best for your business by matching any combination of email, text or phone call to any of the addresses/numbers listed in your profile (2) .

3 . Apply Selections to Multiple Accounts (Optional):

For customers with multiple accounts, select the other accounts to which you want the same preferences applied. You can go back and edit individual accounts at any time (3) .

A detailed overview of setting your notification preferences can be found on the Business Resources page under Preferences and Notifications – Business Customer Guide .

View and Download Usage Data

TRACK AND MANAGE ENERGY USAGE

View and Download Usage Data

Under the Energy Usage tab, you can view analytics of your energy usage – including usage details and graphical views – based on various snapshots of time. Choose from yearly, monthly (bill cycle), weekly or daily – down to 30-minute or 15-minute increments .

Downloadable data allows you to export usage (1) to spreadsheet formats to combine data and integrate it with other data points in your organization .

Note: These snapshots are of individual accounts and may vary based on the meter type for that individual account .

Compare Business Rate Options

Determine whether your accounts are set up on the most favorable rate for your usage patterns . The rate comparison tool allows you to see the differences available rates could make based on your actual usage .

Navigate to the Rate Analysis tool by selecting Usage and Rate Analysis .

Navigate to the Rate Analysis tool by selecting Usage and Rate Analysis .

1 . Select individual meters/accounts to compare rates . Only available and eligible alternative rates will be displayed (1) .

2 . Export the results of the rate analysis to a PDF for

further review (2) .

3 . Call Customer Care or your account executive to

change your rate (3) .

Fast Facts

April 1, 2025

Duke Energy (NYSE: DUK), a Fortune 150 company headquartered in Charlotte, N.C., is one of America’s largest energy holding companies.

The company’s electric utilities serve 8.6 million customers in North Carolina, South Carolina, Florida, Indiana, Ohio and Kentucky, and collectively own approximately 55,100 megawatts of energy capacity. Its natural gas utilities serve 1.7 million customers in North Carolina, South Carolina, Tennessee, Ohio and Kentucky.

Duke Energy is executing an ambitious energy transition, keeping customer reliability and value at the forefront as it builds a smarter energy future. The company is investing in major electric grid upgrades and cleaner generation, including natural gas, nuclear, renewables and energy storage.
